title: Why Is My Vinyl Plank Floor Buckling or Gapping? Expansion Gaps Explained
meta: Vinyl plank buckles when it has no room to expand and gaps when it shrinks or unlocks. Wills Flooring explains the causes in Sammamish homes and each fix.
keywords: vinyl plank floor buckling, why is my vinyl plank floor gapping, LVP expansion gap, vinyl plank lifting in the middle, luxury vinyl plank separating, fix buckled vinyl plank floor

blocks.lead: Vinyl plank buckles because it expanded and had nowhere to go, and it gaps because it shrank or was never fully locked. Both usually trace back to the expansion gap at the walls.
blocks.detail: Floating vinyl plank moves with temperature. Pin it against a wall, a cabinet or a door jamb and the pressure lifts a ridge. Install it cold and tight, then heat the house, and the joints pull apart.

blocks.html: A common Reddit thread goes: "Our vinyl plank was installed last spring and now there is a hump in front of the slider." In Sammamish that slider usually faces south or west over a plateau backyard, the room is a big open-plan main floor in Klahanie or Trossachs, and the plank was sold as waterproof, so the owner assumes it should be indestructible. Water is not the problem. Heat, cold and a floor that cannot move are.

blocks.text: Why a floating floor needs room to move

blocks.html: Click-lock vinyl plank is not attached to the subfloor. Every plank is locked to its neighbors and the whole floor sits as one sheet that grows when it warms and shrinks when it cools. On a 30 ft open-plan room that movement can approach 1/4 in between a January morning and an August afternoon. Manufacturers require a gap at every wall, cabinet, post and door jamb, hidden under the baseboard, so the sheet has somewhere to go. Take that gap away and the energy releases upward.

items.title: Direct sun through big glass
items.text: A south-facing slider in Pine Lake or Beaver Lake can push plank surface temperature past 100 degrees on a July afternoon while the rest of the floor stays at 70. That strip expands faster than everything around it and lifts. Dark planks are worst. Blinds during peak sun help more than anyone wants to hear.

items.title: No gap, or a gap that got filled
items.text: The most common find when we pull a baseboard: planks cut tight to the drywall, or a gap that was later packed with caulk or a bead of construction adhesive under the shoe molding. Either one turns a floating floor into a pinned floor.

items.title: Pinned under a kitchen island or vanity
items.text: Builders in the 1990s and 2000s Sammamish subdivisions often set the island on top of the flooring. A floating floor under 400 lb of cabinet and stone cannot move, so it buckles on the side that gets sun or traffic. Islands and vanities should sit on the subfloor with plank cut around them.

items.title: Subfloor that is not flat
items.text: A hump in the subfloor looks exactly like a buckle. Plank bridging a 1/4 in high spot rocks, the joints open and close, and eventually one pops up. On a crawlspace home this is often a joist crown, not the flooring. See how flat a subfloor needs to be.

blocks.note: Vinyl plank does not gap from water in any normal amount. If the gaps come with soft or spongy spots, the subfloor is the problem and it needs to be looked at.

blocks.text: How we fix a buckled floor in Sammamish

items.text: We pull the baseboard on the two walls closest to the hump and look for tight planks, caulk, adhesive, a nailed transition or a cabinet sitting on the floor.
An oscillating saw trims the plank edge to a 3/8 in gap at the wall. Usually the ridge drops the moment the pressure has somewhere to go.
Planks that lifted often have a crushed locking edge. We disassemble to that row from the wall, swap the damaged planks and re-lock.
items.note: Keep a box of leftovers. Matching a discontinued plank three years later is the hard part.

items.d: Step 4 · Add a transition if the run is too long
items.text: If the room exceeds the manufacturer's maximum, a T-molding at a doorway splits it into two floors that move independently.

items.d: Step 5 · Reinstall trim and check the gap everywhere else
items.text: If one wall was tight, the others probably are too. We check all of them so the buckle does not move to a new spot next summer.

items.html: Screwing or nailing the hump down. The pressure does not disappear; it moves to the next joint and the screw head shows forever.
Caulking the gap at the wall for a cleaner look. Paintable caulk hardens and pins the floor. Shoe molding hides the gap without touching the plank.
Spot gluing a floating plank. A few glued planks create fixed points in a floor designed to move as one sheet. Either fully glue a glue-down product or fully float a click product.
Ignoring it because it is small. A 1/8 in ridge in June is a cracked locking edge by September. Early fixes are cheap.

blocks.title: If your floor was installed in winter:
blocks.text: A floor laid tight in a 60 degree house in January has all of its expansion still ahead of it. The same goes for a Trossachs house left at 50 degrees over the holidays and then heated to 72 in a day. If the first summer brings a hump near the windows, the installer left too little gap. Get it looked at before the second summer does more damage.
What to ask before the next vinyl plank goes in

items: What expansion gap will you leave, and how will you handle the island, the fireplace hearth and the door jambs?
Will the kitchen island and bathroom vanities sit on the subfloor or on the plank?
Where will the transitions go in an open plan, and what is this product's maximum run?
Was the plank acclimated in the room at normal living temperature for 48 hours?
Do I get the leftover boxes? Keep them; a discontinued plank is hard to match later.

faq.q: Can a buckled vinyl plank floor be fixed without replacing it?
faq.a: Usually, yes. If the locking edges are not crushed, cutting the expansion gap back at the nearest walls releases the pressure and the ridge settles. Planks with damaged tongues are swapped from leftover boxes. A full reinstall is only needed when the floor was glued in spots or the subfloor is not flat.

faq.q: How big should the expansion gap be for vinyl plank?
faq.a: Most manufacturers require 1/4 to 3/8 in at every wall, cabinet, post and door jamb. Bigger rooms and sunnier rooms should sit at the larger end. The gap is hidden by baseboard or shoe molding and must never be filled with caulk, adhesive or grout.

faq.q: Will the gaps in my vinyl plank close on their own?
faq.a: Small, even end-joint gaps that appeared in winter often close when the house warms in spring, especially in a plateau home with big windows. A single wide gap on one plank will not close; that joint was never fully locked and needs to be re-engaged from the nearest wall.

faq.q: Is buckling covered by the flooring warranty?
faq.a: Almost never. Manufacturer warranties exclude installation errors, and a missing expansion gap is the textbook installation error. That is why the installer's workmanship warranty matters. Wills Flooring backs every installation with a 1-year workmanship warranty and comes back if a gap was left short.

faq.q: Does direct sunlight really buckle vinyl plank?
faq.a: Yes. A sunny strip in front of a south-facing slider can run 30 degrees hotter than the rest of the room. That strip expands faster and lifts against the cooler planks around it. Rigid SPC planks, a proper gap and blinds during peak sun keep it flat.

faq.q: How much does it cost to re-lay a vinyl plank floor?
faq.a: Wills Flooring installs vinyl plank at $2.50 per sq ft in labor with a 500 sq ft minimum, and we can often reuse the existing planks if they are undamaged. Small repairs that only need the gap cut back are quoted separately at the free estimate and are far cheaper than a re-lay.
